commitResults.messageBody:
CoordiMate has no event workflow, leaving organizers without a way to
create and review events.

Add addevent with date and time validation, unique names, and persistent
storage. Require chronological start and end times; compare dates alone
when either time is omitted. Add an Events view with selected event
details and compact, clear command feedback.

with tests.

requiring a graphical display that the provided Linux CI workflow does
not configure. It also exceeded its timeout when run through WSL.

Developers will manually verify event UI behavior when making UI changes.

Add tests for event storage conversion and validation, including
missing fields, invalid event details, duplicate names, null list
entries, and round-trip preservation of events.

Treat event names that differ only by case as duplicates, while preserving
the capitalization entered by the user for display. This improves the
user experience, since a user might not intend case differences to result
in two distinct events.
Add event management to CoordiMate

Events cannot be changed after creation, making corrections difficult.

Add editevent to update an event’s name, start time, or end time while
retaining omitted fields. Match names without regard to case and reject
duplicate names or invalid time ranges.

Save edits through the existing persistence flow so a failed save leaves
the event unchanged. Document the command and cover parsing, behavior,
and integration with tests.

commitResults.messageTitle: Clarify command errors and include usage
commitResults.messageBody:
Command errors can omit the failing field or prefix, show unrelated
examples, and provide inconsistent guidance. This makes it difficult
to identify and correct invalid input.

Identify empty fields and unknown or repeated prefixes explicitly.
Use examples matching the supplied parameter and separate length errors
for event names and tags. Append the relevant command usage once to
parse, execution, and storage errors.

Use a shared saved-data loading message across command types. Update
the guides and regression tests to cover the revised messages,
parameter-specific examples, and usage appearing exactly once.

Validation: all 723 tests and both Checkstyle checks pass.

Event times preserve optional times but lack typed accessors for
reminder checks. Upcoming reminders need consistent timing and ordering.

Add typed date and optional date-time accessors, and find upcoming
events using an injected clock. Include both 24-hour window boundaries
and date-only events throughout their local start date. Order results
by start time and then by name, using midnight for date-only ordering.

Test boundaries, local timezones, daylight saving changes, and ordering
without real-time waits. All 773 tests, Checkstyle, and coverage
verification pass with gradlew check.

Events have no persistent reminder dismissal history.
Rebuilding an event for an edit would otherwise lose its
dismissed schedules.

Store dismissed start values with each event and load older
JSON files with an empty history. Preserve history through
event edits, roster changes, attendance updates, and contact
renames or deletion.

Keep date-only and timed starts distinct, and retain earlier
dismissed schedules so reverting a start does not revive its
reminder. Include history in event equality while retaining
name-based identity.

Add 25 tests for persistence, compatibility, schedule changes,
and command integration. All 798 tests, Checkstyle, and
coverage verification pass with gradlew check.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add reminder management and dismissal saving
commitResults.messageBody:
Eligibility and dismissal history exist, but Logic has no API
for presenting active reminders or saving their dismissal.

Expose a live reminder list, explicit refresh, and dismissal
through Logic. Refresh after commands and use an injected
clock to evaluate eligibility without storage access.

Save dismissal history before updating the model. On a load
or save error, keep suppression in memory and report that the
reminder may reappear after restarting. Preserve temporary
dismissals across renames and discard them on event deletion.

Ignore repeated dismissals and outdated reminder snapshots.
Add 20 integration tests covering refresh, persistence,
failures, event changes, and restart. All 818 tests, Checkstyle,
and coverage verification pass with gradlew check.

commitResults.messageBody:
Reminder logic is available, but the desktop window has no
reminder display or periodic eligibility checks.

Add a shared reminder panel above the workspace tabs with saved

startup and every minute using a JavaFX Timeline. Show failed
save warnings while retaining session-only dismissal behavior.

Keep the panel bounded and the sidebar scrollable so the
workspace and command input remain usable at the minimum size.
Support keyboard dismissal and preserve focus as rows disappear.
Stop the timer and detach listeners when the window closes or
the application shuts down.

Add 14 tests for UI behavior and shutdown. All 832 tests,

Inspect desktop, minimum-window, and warning-state snapshots;
the post-implementation UI audit passes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show date-only reminders today and tomorrow
commitResults.messageBody:
Date-only reminders appear only on the event's start date.
Members need the preceding calendar day to prepare as well.

Include date-only events throughout the day before their start
and the start date itself. Keep the timed-event window unchanged.
Use local calendar dates so daylight saving changes do not alter
the date-only reminder window.

Cover midnight boundaries, leap days, year changes, daylight
saving, live refresh, saved dismissals, and the displayed dates.

All 835 tests, Checkstyle, and coverage verification pass with

Dismissal history suppresses previously used start values even

Reset saved dismissal history when an event's start changes.
Discard temporary session suppression when its start changes
too. Keep dismissal for unchanged starts, name or end-only
edits, and failed schedule saves.

Cover reversion, restart, date-only and timed starts, legacy
history, failed writes, and reverting to a past start. Keep
past events excluded by the existing eligibility rules.

commitResults.messageBody:
New contacts need model-owned IDs that survive in-memory changes.

Allocate IDs centrally, preserve allocation state across model copies,
and reject duplicate IDs independently of contact detail checks. Reserve
existing IDs before assigning missing IDs during bulk replacement, and
reject exhausted allocation without changing data.

commitResults.messageTitle: Persist member IDs and migrate legacy data
commitResults.messageBody:
Member IDs and allocation state only survive in memory, so restarting
can change IDs and reuse the identifiers of deleted members.

Save each member ID and the next available ID in JSON. Reserve existing
IDs before allocating missing ones in legacy or mixed records. Reject
duplicate IDs, invalid numbers, and inconsistent allocation state.

Restore full persistence equality assertions, cover repeated restarts
and migration, and document the saved ID fields in the user guide.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject year zero in event dates
commitResults.messageBody:
Event date validation accepts year 0000 through Java's ISO date
parsing, although the conventional BC/AD calendar has no year zero.

Require a positive year in the shared EventTime validator so adding
and editing events enforce the same restriction. State the valid
year range in the validation error.

Add regression tests for start and end dates with optional times,
unchanged model and file contents after rejection, storage validation,
and round trips for years 0001 and 9999.

Validation: gradlew check passes with 1,076 tests, Checkstyle, and
coverage verification.

commitResults.messageTitle: Remove saved year-zero events at startup
commitResults.messageBody:
Saved events with year 0000 prevent the data file from loading under
the positive-year validation rule, hiding otherwise valid data.

Delete affected events during startup and notify the user afterward
with their names. Include year-zero dates in reminder history so they
do not prevent the remaining data from loading.

Validate the remaining data before saving it atomically. Leave the
original file unchanged if validation or saving fails, and report the
cleanup failure without claiming that events were deleted.

Add tests for startup cleanup, preserved data, repeated startup,
failure handling, and the notification shown after the window opens.

Validation: gradlew check passes with 1,083 tests, Checkstyle, and
coverage verification.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix date-only and mixed event durations
commitResults.messageBody:
The details pane hides durations whenever either endpoint lacks a time.
Date-only events need an inclusive count, while mixed inputs need a
message identifying the missing time.

Use EventTime values to count calendar dates inclusively and identify
the missing endpoint time. Cover same-day events, month and year
boundaries, leap day, and both mixed-input directions in UI tests.

commitResults.messageTitle: Format timed durations in days, hours and minutes
commitResults.messageBody:
Timed durations appear entirely in hours and minutes, making longer
events hard to read. Zero-length and sub-hour events also show an
unnecessary hours unit.

Split elapsed time into 24-hour days, hours and minutes. Omit zero
units, preserve singular and plural forms, and show 0 minutes for
identical timestamps. Cover full days, partial days, short durations,
and month and year boundaries in UI tests.

The user guide lists duration as an event detail without explaining
how optional times affect it.

Describe inclusive date-only counts, elapsed timed durations using
24-hour days, and missing-time messages for mixed inputs. Include
examples for all three cases and explain zero units and timestamps.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test duration refresh after selection and edits
commitResults.messageBody:
Duration tests exercise each format in a fresh details pane, leaving
stale text after selection changes or timestamp edits unchecked.

Cover switching between date-only, timed and mixed-input events, and
replacing the selected event as its timestamps change. Check the
selected event, duration and displayed timestamps together.
Fix event duration display

commitResults.messageTitle: Preserve events with year-zero reminder history
commitResults.messageBody:
Startup cleanup deletes an entire event when only its dismissed
reminder history contains a year-zero date. This also loses members
and attendance.

Remove year-zero reminder entries from otherwise valid events and
save the cleaned data. Keep deleting events whose start or end date
uses year zero. Add regression coverage for both cleanup paths.
Disallow year 0000 for Events

commitResults.messageTitle: Show member leave status in event details
commitResults.messageBody:
Assigned members show contact details and attendance, but their leave
status is only visible in Contacts. Event planning needs the same
availability information.

Show the existing leave label beneath the role of each member when
leave covers today. Use the contact source so filtered members remain
visible, and retain attendance as a separate status.

Verify current, ended, missing, edited, and cleared leave in UI tests.

commitResults.messageTitle: Refresh event leave indicators after midnight
commitResults.messageBody:
An open Events view retains the leave indicator until a contact or
event changes, even after the last day of leave has passed.

Share the window clock with the Events view and refresh its selected
event on date changes through the existing minute timer. Keep the
selection and attendance intact and avoid rebuilding rows each minute.

Exercise expiry through the window timer and verify leave labels fit
beside attendance and long notes at narrow and desktop widths.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document leave status in the Events view
commitResults.messageBody:
The guide describes leave only in Contacts, leaving event planners
without instructions for the leave indicator in assigned member rows.

Describe current leave in event details, its automatic expiry, and
its independence from event dates and attendance counts.

commitResults.messageTitle: Refresh leave status when reopening the window
commitResults.messageBody:
A window reopened after midnight retains expired leave indicators until
the next minute tick.

Refresh both leave views when the window is shown, using the existing
date checks and minute timer.

Add a regression test for reopening across midnight. Exercise event
creation, assignment, attendance and leave edits through the command
box, and verify failed saves preserve the displayed and saved state.
Check that expiry itself does not rewrite the data file.

commitResults.messageTitle: Cover leave expiry across dates and archives
commitResults.messageBody:
Leave status depends on the local date and the full saved roster.
Date changes and hidden contacts need coverage to protect event
indicators and attendance.

Test mixed expiry dates, backward clock changes and archived events
whose members are hidden by archive state and contact filters. Verify
that clearing leave updates the selected event without changing its
attendance or selection.
